questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of Linear First-Order Equations?
questions.answer: A linear first-order ODE contains the unknown function and its first derivative only to the first power. The integrating factor turns the left side into the derivative of a product.

questions.prompt: Solve y prime plus 2y equals 6 for a thermal offset y.
questions.answer: Here p(x)=2 and q(x)=6. The integrating factor is \[\mu=e^{\int2\,dx}=e^{2x}\] Multiply the ODE by e^{2x}: \[e^{2x}y'+2e^{2x}y=6e^{2x}\] The left side is a product derivative: \[(e^{2x}y)'=6e^{2x}\] Integrate: \[e^{2x}y=3e^{2x}+C\] so \[y=3+Ce^{-2x}\]

questions.prompt: Put dq/dt plus q over RC equals V over R into integrating-factor form.
questions.answer: The dependent variable is q(t). Here p(t)=1/(RC) and q(t) on the right is the source V/R, not the charge. The integrating factor is \[\mu(t)=e^{\int 1/(RC)\,dt}=e^{t/(RC)}\] Multiplying gives \[(e^{t/(RC)}q)'=e^{t/(RC)}\frac{V}{R}\] which can then be integrated.
